articleTitle: SOCRATES: System Of Cellular RAdio for Traffic Efficiency and Safety
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: SOCRATES is a multinational research project investigating the use of cellular radio for a complete system of RTI, including dynamic route guidance and many other applications. It is developing techniques for using cellular radio as the basic communication medium. Many RTI applications will depend upon the widespread availability of two-way communication between vehicles and control centres; cellular radio offers a potential pan-European infrastructure which should provide an economically efficient basis for the Integrated Road Transport Environment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An open architecture for RTI applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: There is now a significant effort to apply electronic engineering, information technology and telecommunications to develop alternative approaches to improve the overall efficiency of the vehicle, its driver and passengers. This is a very new market with little hard commercial evidence of the demand for the various services that could be provided. The initial systems are addressing specific requirements (e.g. road tolls) and engineered for the minimum cost to achieve a specific function. The applications are tightly coupled to the chosen communications system. Several incompatible implementations of the same functionality emerge. However, as the number of services available increases the user may want access to several such services packaged into a single terminal.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Problems and opportunities of nonstop vehicle recognition
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: The author considers the factors that make non-stop toll collection/road pricing different from traditional toll collection and a rationale for developing a product range to meet these requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The challenges of using GPS NAVSTAR satellite navigation for vehicle location
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: The technology of the Global Positioning System is summarized with regard to the requirements of a vehicle location system which is seen to demand additional inputs related to vehicular motion. Infrastructural and integrational issues remaining to be resolved are highlighted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New techniques for highway network data collection and presentation-the Doncaster HIVP experience
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: This paper describes the experience of a UK local government highway authority in the quest to apply information technology to the task of network-wide data collection and management. The innovative techniques adopted have equal relevance for the construction of practical and consistent navigation databases. This paper also covers the development of such techniques for the collection of network attributes for route guidance and navigation systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microwave link data communication between a moving vehicle and a roadside beacon
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: This link has been developed within the European DRIVE Programme, to implement an automatic debiting system for the PAMELA project. It will enable tolls to be collected without the requirement for vehicles to slow down or be confined to lanes. The features of the link, as designed, are the localised communication area, the small size and low cost of the vehicle-mounted unit, and the capacity to operate with a short communication time. The passive transponder allows close control of the operating range, without vehicle-to-vehicle interference, and has the advantage of an extremely simple microwave front end. Implemented as a microstrip circuit, this can be accommodated within the outline of a credit card including all microwave transmit and receive components.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: This paper includes toll collection, both fixed payment and payment by length of journey, road pricing in various forms, and the concepts of congestion charging. It outlines the general requirements of each system, and particularly highlights the various features which involve specific aspects of technology to be covered by later papers of this Colloquium.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Data transmission for dynamic route guidance and road pricing
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: This paper discusses the role of roadside beacon-to-vehicle communication systems to achieve information transfer/transactions using distributed beacons. It concentrates on beacon-based infrastructures only, examining some conclusions from work undertaken in the DRG & RP fields, and assesses the requirements for the in-vehicle-equipment and roadside-to-vehicle communications performance. It also examines the communications architecture and protocols to achieve these requirements, potential pitfalls for the standardisation process, and possible methods of avoiding them.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Route guidance information by beacons or radio
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: This paper presents an assessment of leading technology options for providing route guidance and information to drivers. It builds on work being carried out within the EC DRIVE RDS-ALERT project, towards pan-European standardization of the Radio Data System Traffic Message Channel. It also draws on the results of a study carried out for the Rijkswaterstaat on dynamic route guidance systems for the Amsterdam metropolitan area.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: International mobile satellite communications for the transport industry
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: INMARSAT, operating four geostationary satellites with worldwide coverage, was originally intended for merchant ships, but now addresses the marine, land mobile, portable and aviation international markets. INMARSAT-C is a small, low power terminal ideal for fitting in vehicles such as trucks and cars. The relative simplicity of the INMARSAT-C system means that data, at 600 bit/s, is the only means of communicating, but INMARSAT have designed some innovative protocols into the specification which allow data reporting, polling and group calling, as well as standard messaging.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: System integrity and user verification of integrity (road pricing and route guidance)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: The author concludes that technical innovation and excellence alone will not ensure success; both operator and user must be provided with adequate means of verifying the integrity of the system. The user should be permitted to interrogate the system for this purpose, and where such 'hands-on' verification is not possible an independent assessment must be permitted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Creating a digital road network for Europe: experience from the PANDORA project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Technology for Road Pricing and Route Guidance
abstract: The Automobile Association, Ordnance Survey, Philips BV and Robert Bosch GmbH have collaborated in a DRIVE project to create and test a prototype navigation database. The data requirements of future vehicle navigation systems were examined. Digital street networks were extracted mainly from Ordnance Survey's large-scale digital mapping and the necessary road and traffic attributes were collected by the AA. These data were integrated into a specially designed prototype database for parts of London and Birmingham and the major interconnecting roads. Data were abstracted from the database and supplied to Bosch and Philips using the GDF standard developed in the DEMETER project. This dataset was then tested in field trials using prototype systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
